definition: The first amendment to the U.S. Constitution, which prohibits Congress — and, through the Fourteenth Amendment, state governments — from abridging freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, and the right to petition. It is the central constitutional provision at issue in this case.
examples: Petitioners argue that when a therapist speaks with a patient during a session, that conversation is protected speech under the First Amendment that the government cannot simply ban because it dislikes the message.
